1.

Through the instant petition, filed by the petitioner seeks anticipatory bail in case FIR No. 76 dated 17.08.2024 registered under Sections 406, 420 of IPC (Section 201 of IPC added later on)
registered at Police Station Bhargo Camp, District Police Commissionerate, Jalandhar.

2. Learned State counsel has filed status report by way of an affidavit of Harshpreet Singh, PPS,
Assistant Commissioner of Police, West, Jalandhar on behalf of respondent-State in Court, which is taken on record, accordingly to which the petitioner has joined the investigation on 09.11.2024.
3.
Vide order dated 04.11.2024, passed by this Court, the petitioner was released on interim bail and was directed to join investigation.

Order dated 04.11.2024, passed by this Court, reads as under:
"CRM-43212-2024 This application has been filed by the petitioner for addition of offence under Section 201 of IPC by submitting that due to inadvertent mistake,
aforementioned section could not be added in [attest to the accuracy and the head note as well as prayer clause of the main petition.
integrity of this document CRM-M-53298-2024
For the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed and offence under Section 201 of IPC is ordered to be added in the head note as well as prayer clause of the main petition.
Registry is directed to make the necessary correction.
Application stands disposed of.

sentences.text: Main case

The instant petition has been filed seeking benefit of pre- arrest bail in case arising out of FIR No.76 dated 17.08.2024 under Sections 406, 420 of IPC (Section 201 of IPC added later on) registered at Police Station Bhargo Camp District Police Comissionerate, Jalandhar, Punjab on the basis of a written complaint filed by the complainant-Joginder Singh alleging therein that his daughter Rajwinder Kaur was married to Manpreet Singh, who is son of the present petitioner, on 05.12.2022.

entities.text: Police Station Bhargo Camp District Police Comissionerate, Jalandhar, Punjab
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The son of the petitioner was working abroad and 15 days after the wedding, he had gone back.
The daughter of the complainant had to join him.
On 02.02.2023, she suffered a heart attack when she had come to the house of the complainant for the purpose of submission of her visa application and had died.

On request of Manpreet Singh to the effect that he needed money for starting some business, the complainant transferred an amount of Rs.15 lakhs in the bank account of his mother-in-law i.e present petitioner.
The present petitioner had assured him to return that amount within a period of three months.

The complainant also alleged that he had spent huge money at the time of marriage of her daughter as istridhan and cash amount of Rs.4,50,000/- had also been given to the co-accused Manpreet Singh who is the husband of her daughter, for the purpose of submitting paper of his daughter in the embassy, had also not been returned.
The complainant has prayed for taking action against the petitioner and his family members.
Apprehending her arrest, the petitioner moved an application for grant of pre-arrest bail which was dismissed by learned Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Jalandhar vide order dated 10.10.2024.
It is argued by learned counsel for the petitioner that she has been falsely implicated in this case.
There is delay of one year and nine months in registration of FIR from the date of death of daughter of the complainant.

The amount of Rs.15 lakhs was transferred in the bank account of the petitioner by the complainant as that much CRM-M-53298-2024 2024 POH TG 38 amount was due qua him towards the son of the petitioner.
The said amount had not been borrowed by the petitioner or his son as has been alleged and that dispute between the parties is even otherwise a civil nature.
She is ready to join the investigation.
Her custodial investigation is not required.
No recovery is to be effected from her.
Therefore, it is urged that she deserves to be extended benefit of bail.
Notice of motion.
At this stage, Power of Attorney has been filed on behalf of the complainant.

Learned State counsel assisted by learned counsel for the complainant has submitted that there are serious allegations against the petitioner who in connivance with her son had induced the complainant to part with sum of Rs.15 lakhs by way of loan and the same would be returned within a period of three months.
It is also argued that the petitioner has joined investigation but she has not cooperated with the investigation that is why her application for pre- arrest bail was rejected.
It is therefore, urged that petitioner does not deserve to be extended benefit of pre-arrest bail.

2 I n t h e m e a n t i m e , t h e p e t i t i o n e r i s d i r e c t e d t o a p p e a r b e f o r e t h e Investigating/Arresting Officer to join investigation within one week or as and when s u b s e q u e n t l y r e q u i r e d t h e r e a f t e r . I n t h e e v e n t o f h e r a r r e s t , t h e Investigating/Arresting Officer shall release the petitioner on interim bail on furnishing personal/surety bonds to his/her satisfaction.

sentences.text: The petitioner shall also abide by the conditions as envisaged under Section 482 (2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (for short BNSS), 2023."
4. Learned State counsel, on instructions from the Investigating Officer, has submitted that the petitioner has joined investigation on 09.11.2024 and he is not required for custodial interrogation.

5. Keeping in view the above mentioned facts and circumstances, without commenting on the merits of the case, the present petition is allowed MOHIT ei and the order dated 04.11.2024, granting interim bail to the petitioner, is MOHIT 2024.12.13 16:16 2024 BHC TGG8 made absolute, subject to the conditions laid down in Section 482(2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023.
